parts.label: On, hover and focus of an item

steps.why: Things that belong together sit close.

steps.pick: radius.2: We use a 2px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls and keep density. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough to read as an object, while it keeps straight lines that align in rows. So a dense toolbar reads as one line of actions, because the product is dense (content.q2) and precise (brand.q1), with slightly rounded controls (shape.values).

steps.question: What is the smallest target?
steps.why: Mouse and keyboard; compact targets are enough.
Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.

steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Small corners keep dense rows straight.
Small corners keep dense rows straight.
